name: Palt Typesetting
category: A4. Vector, typography, diagrams and stills
role: Japanese and Latin typesetting markup: thin spaces at script boundaries, word-break spans, palt CSS
summary: palt-typesetting turns a string or DOM element of Japanese and mixed Japanese-Latin text into spans that carry quarter-em spacing between scripts, optional per-pair kerning and word-boundary line breaks, for a stylesheet that sets font-feature-settings palt. render() runs in Node through jsdom and is deterministic. It does not shape text or apply palt itself: the proportional narrowing comes from the browser and a font with a palt feature, so a scene that uses it must be captured in a browser.
use_when: Japanese and Latin titles or captions in a browser-captured scene needing tight kana and script-boundary spacing
Deterministic HTML for Japanese copy in a Playwright scene with a pinned Noto Sans JP
avoid_when: satori, resvg or canvas text, where the spans and CSS do nothing; use harfbuzz
Needing the spacing numbers without a browser: shape with harfbuzz and the font's palt feature
notes: 2026-11-27: lead said it applies palt spacing; the 0.9.5 source and README show it only wraps text and sets classes, palt itself is CSS font-feature-settings. README is Japanese.
2026-11-27: font used is @fontsource/noto-sans-jp 5.3.1, OFL-1.1, redistributable. Its fontsource files are unicode-range slices, so load the text with document.fonts.load before measuring.
2026-11-27: two predeclared checks are KNOWN FAIL in the example: palt widened 3 of 33 characters by up to 0.7 px, and 「 is already half-width without palt (Chromium text-spacing-trim).

assessment.rationale: npm palt-typesetting 0.9.5 published 2026-10-25, MIT, repository pushed 2026-11-09. Dependencies jsdom and linebreak. harfbuzz, opentype-js and troika-three-text shape glyphs but add no Japanese composition rules. The lead's claim of applying palt is wrong: it supplies markup and CSS, and the font does the narrowing. Browser capture only, so a niche tool.

evidence.result: Partial: render() and PNG identical across runs, 6 thin spaces inserted, palt narrows a 33-character line 1326.3 px to 1181.72 px (-10.9%) with Noto Sans JP 5.3.1. KNOWN FAIL: palt widened 3 characters by up to 0.7 px; 「 already half-width without palt.
evidence.scope: One Japanese and Latin sentence, Noto Sans JP 400 via fontsource, Chromium via Playwright, macOS arm64; not other fonts, kerningRules, word break or browsers
